subject: Post-call: data residency & isolation — Dedicated vs Private VPC options
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Voss <tara@clearhealth.com>, Andrew Lin <andrew@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: data residency & isolation — Dedicated vs Private VPC options

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate the clarity on your security and regulatory guardrails. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Key takeaways from today’s discovery:
- Data types: training/analytics pipelines include de-identified datasets, but live inference will touch PHI and patient identifiers in a narrow set of endpoints.
- Residency: production inference must persist logs and audit trails within a US-only boundary; control plane metadata must meet your internal retention policy.
- KMS: you prefer customer-managed keys (BYOK) when possible.
- Network: strong preference for network isolation and private peering; public-hosted endpoints would require additional compensating controls.

Qualification questions we need to close on before the technical deep-dive:
1) Control plane residency: do you require the Redwood control plane to be customer-managed (on-prem) or is a VPC-deployed private control plane acceptable?
2) KMS posture: BYOK (HSM/KMS in your cloud) vs Redwood-managed keys — which is a blocker vs a negotiable requirement?
3) Audit/logging frequency: are sub-minute audit exports required, or will hourly exports be sufficient for the initial rollout?
4) Egress and network topology: do you require strict non-routable egress from inference nodes to the public internet?

Quick mapping of options (high-level):
- Hosted API: fastest to launch, but typically fails your BYOK/control-plane residency constraints.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools in Redwood’s tenant with strict tenancy isolation — can be configured with some network restrictions and exported audit logs; BYOK possible depending on the control plane residency needs.
- Private VPC (customer VPC or on-prem): full tenancy + networking control, customer-managed KMS, and private control plane — higher integration time.

Next steps I propose:
- Tara/Andrew: reply inline with answers to the four questions above (or confirm which are deal-breakers).
- Redwood: we’ll attach a short SOC 2 extract and a KMS architecture diagram for your infra team to review.
- If aligned, schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra engs and your cloud security team next week (60–90 min).

Attachments: clearhealth-soc2-extract.pdf (SOC 2: relevant sections), redwood-kms-diagram.png (illustrative BYOK flows).

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Account Manager | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Tara Voss <tara@clearhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Andrew Lin <andrew@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: data residency & isolation — Dedicated vs Private VPC options

Thanks Neha — quick clarifications from our side (Tara, CISO):
- PHI: yes, inference requests will include PHI for the pilot (consented patients). That makes BYOK + private control plane a hard requirement unless you can demonstrate equivalent cryptographic separation and legal controls.
- Control plane: our preference is a Private VPC with a customer-facing control plane that sits in our AWS account. Dedicated capacity inside Redwood’s tenancy is acceptable only if the control plane and audit ingestion can be routed into our account (no persistent metadata held outside of our region).
- Audit logs: we require near-real-time audit exports (<= 5 minutes) for action events during the pilot.
- Network: inference nodes must not have direct public egress; all outbound traffic must route through our NAT/proxy and IDS.

If you can confirm the following pieces we can move to the technical deep-dive:
1) Evidence of successful BYOK integrations with customer KMS (example references or diagrams).
2) Example audit export cadence and format (sample JSON lines is fine).
3) Confirmation on egress controls and whether Redwood supports transit through a customer VPC/NAT gateway.

On timing: we’re available Tue/Wed next week for a 90-min session with our infra and network security engineers.

—Tara
Tara Voss
Chief Information Security Officer
ClearHealth
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Voss <tara@clearhealth.com>, Andrew Lin <andrew@clearhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 13:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: data residency & isolation — Dedicated vs Private VPC options

Tara — thank you, that’s very helpful. Short answers inline, plus plan:

1) BYOK: Redwood supports BYOK flows with both cloud KMS providers and customer HSM via an ephemeral key exchange pattern. I’ve attached a short KMS diagram (redwood-kms-diagram.png) showing the flow we discussed — we’ll also include two reference customers who used BYOK in a PII/PHI environment in the tech deep-dive (we’ll anonymize logs).

2) Audit exports: we support push-based audit exports with sub-60s granularity; we can easily configure to a <=5 minute push to an S3 bucket or Kinesis stream in your account, delivered as JSON lines. We’ll include a sample output in the drive link.

3) Egress controls: Private VPC deployments can route egress through your NAT/proxy—no direct public egress required. For Dedicated (Redwood-managed tenancy) we can implement strict egress firewalling and proxying, but routing through your VPC requires Private control plane or peering.

Tradeoffs (brief):
- Private VPC (your account): strongest guarantees for BYOK, network control, and audit residency; integration time ~4–6 weeks for Prod-facing pipeline.
- Dedicated: faster (~2–3 weeks) and lower integration lift; may need additional control-plane routing work to meet your BYOK/residency demands.

Next step: propose Tue 2026-07-14 10:00–11:30 PT for the technical deep-dive. Please confirm attendees and I’ll send a calendar invite + agenda.

Neha
Neha Kapoor | Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL — ClearHealth: ask list & prep for technical deep-dive (Tue 7/14)

Internal notes (do not forward to customer):

Summary of requirements from Tara: BYOK (customer KMS/HSM), <=5m audit push to customer-owned stream, no direct public egress (route through customer NAT), control plane metadata residency in their account preferred.

Action items for Tuesday session:
- Marissa: prepare a 10-slide ops slide that shows two deployment patterns (Private VPC in customer account vs Dedicated with control-plane peering). Highlight time-to-prod and required infra changes. (Slides + one diagram)
- Karthik: prepare a short demo plan for BYOK exchange (key lifecycle, rotation, HSM integration notes). Bring two anonymized reference logs (JSON lines) showing audit events and export cadence.
- Neha: I’ll own the agenda, invite list, and attach the SOC2 excerpt + KMS diagram. I’ll also draft the mutual action plan (MAP) with timelines for both paths so Tara can pick a route.

Risks to flag: dedicated path may require a temporary legal attestation if full control-plane residency in their account is non-trivial; we should have a fallback checklist for compensating controls. Also confirm which Redwood infra owner will be on the call (ops lead + infra eng).

I’ll send the Tech Deep-dive invite after I hear back on attendee names (I already tentatively booked 10:00–11:30 PT Tue 7/14).

Neha
